SMTO-CFG-0086 — SMTO needs your OK before using this Skill

GUID: 5e913dad-98b0-5dc4-bd94-cb435edad44b
Slug: capability-activation-explicit-user-trigger-required
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • This Skill only turns on when you allow it. SMTO's Agent wants to use it, so SMTO is asking you first. Nothing has been done with the Skill yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Task, find the Capability permission required question and read which Skill it names. The question shows exactly which Skill the Agent wants to turn on.
  2. Select Allow for this task (or Allow for this conversation, if that is the choice shown) to let SMTO use the Skill, or Don't allow if you don't. Your answer is the permission this Skill needs, and the Task waits until you choose.
  3. If you want SMTO to use this Skill whenever it helps without asking, open Capabilities by the message box and set it to Always. A Skill set to Always is included in every request, so SMTO no longer has to stop and ask.

What success looks like

  • After you allow it, a Capability use allowed note appears and the Task continues; after Don't allow, the Task continues without that Skill.

If it still fails

  • If the question doesn't appear or your answer isn't accepted, send Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO. Use the buttons rather than typing a reply; a typed reply that isn't a clear yes or no grants nothing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Activation of an explicit_only Skill inside the accepted ceiling requires a recorded user trigger for the current task source; the runtime opened a capability grant question and paused the run.

What this means

  • A Skill marked explicit_only is inside accepted authority but lacks a recorded user trigger for the current source digest. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • A Skill marked explicit_only is inside accepted authority but lacks a recorded user trigger for the current source digest.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the runtime-issued grant/question and current task intent, separate from general permission and credentials.

How to fix it

  • Answer the run's Capability permission required wait through the clarification endpoint with the runtime-issued capability_grant_request_id and a decision of allow or deny (open_capability_requirement in src/agent_runtime/native/authority_control.py; answer_in in src/agent_runtime/native/capability_grants.py). Don't synthesize triggers; adding the Skill to always_skill_ids pre-selects it for future runs.
  • Ask the user whether to use this capability, using the runtime-issued capability question ID.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • The matching explicit user trigger is accepted through the existing interaction boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
